014package org.microbean.bean;
015
016import java.util.ArrayList;
017import java.util.List;
018
019import java.util.function.BiFunction;
020
021import static java.util.Collections.unmodifiableList;
022
023import static org.microbean.bean.Ranked.DEFAULT_RANK;
024
025public class RankedReducer<C, T extends Ranked> implements Reducer<C, T> {
026
027  public RankedReducer() {
028    super();
029  }
030
031  @Override
032  public T reduce(final List<? extends T> elements,
033                  final C c,
034                  final BiFunction<? super List<? extends T>, ? super C, ? extends T> failureHandler) {
035    if (elements == null || elements.isEmpty()) {
036      return null;
037    } else if (elements.size() == 1) {
038      return elements.get(0);
039    }
040
041    T candidate = null;
042    List<T> unresolved = null;
043    // Highest rank wins
044    int maxRank = DEFAULT_RANK;
045
046    for (final T element : elements) {
047      if (element.alternate()) {
048        final int elementRank = element.rank();
049        if (elementRank == maxRank) {
050          if (candidate == null || !candidate.alternate()) {
051            // Prefer elements regardless of ranks.
052            candidate = element;
053          } else {
054            assert candidate.rank() == maxRank : "Unexpected rank: " + candidate.rank() + "; was expecting: " + maxRank;
055            // The existing candidate is an alternate and by definition has the highest rank we've seen so far; the
056            // incoming element is also an alternate; both have equal ranks: we can't resolve this.
057            if (unresolved == null) {
058              unresolved = new ArrayList<>(6);
059            }
060            unresolved.add(candidate);
061            unresolved.add(element);
062            candidate = null;
063          }
064        } else if (elementRank > maxRank) {
065          if (candidate == null || !candidate.alternate() || elementRank > candidate.rank()) {
066            // The existing candidate is either null, not an alternate (and alternates are always preferred), or an
067            // alternate with losing rank, so junk it in favor of the incoming element.
068            candidate = element;
069            // We have a new maxRank.
070            maxRank = elementRank;
071          } else if (elementRank == candidate.rank()) {
072            // The existing candidate is also an alternate and has the same rank.
073            if (unresolved == null) {
074              unresolved = new ArrayList<>(6);
075            }
076            unresolved.add(candidate);
077            unresolved.add(element);
078            candidate = null;
079          } else {
080            assert elementRank < candidate.rank() : "elementRank >= candidate.rank(): " + elementRank + " >= " + candidate.rank();
081            // The existing candidate is also an alternate but has a higher rank than the alternate, so keep it (do
082            // nothing).
083          }
084        }
085        // ...else drop element by doing nothing
086      } else if (candidate == null) {
087        // The incoming element is not an alternate, but that doesn't matter; the candidate is null, so accept the
088        // element no matter what.
089        candidate = element;
090      } else if (!candidate.alternate()) {
091        // The existing candidate is not an alternate. The incoming element is not an alternate. Ranks in this case are
092        // irrelevant, perhaps surprisingly. We cannot resolve this.
093        if (unresolved == null) {
094          unresolved = new ArrayList<>(6);
095        }
096        unresolved.add(candidate);
097        unresolved.add(element);
098        candidate = null;
099      }
100      // ...else do nothing
101    }
102
103    if (unresolved != null && !unresolved.isEmpty()) {
104      if (candidate != null) {
105        unresolved.add(candidate);
106      }
107      candidate =
108        failureHandler == null ? Reducer.fail(unmodifiableList(unresolved), c) : failureHandler.apply(unmodifiableList(unresolved), c);
109    }
110
111    return candidate;
112  }
113
114}
